claims.statement: The feature definition makes the multiple-account workstation guide available for FPT/GHEC, not GHES. macOS, Windows and Linux sections describe HTTPS credential separation, not automatic target validation.

HTTPS separation uses per-account PATs and repository-path credential caching. Classic PAT examples use repo scope; fine-grained alternatives bind account/organization desired repositories and read/write contents. Source examples do not authorize new credentials or maximal privileges.

The helper check reads credential.helper, then branches by configured helper; absence of a recognized helper skips stored-helper clearing. macOS keychain, Git Credential Manager and Windows wincred require distinct erasure mechanisms.

Credential erasure examples target host-level GitHub credentials and can disrupt other repositories/accounts. The Windows GCM snippet uses backtick-n while the macOS/Linux snippet uses backslash-n; shell-specific syntax needs independent validation, not blind execution.

The useHttpPath global configuration caches credentials by full remote repository URL; initial repository access prompts for the authorized account PAT. Cached configuration is not proof of correct credential identity or permission scope.

The GIT_SSH_COMMAND wrapper alternative determines repository owner/name from origin, selects the correct key and configures SSH; its example specifies IdentitiesOnly and a key path. Arbitrary remote strings are not trusted identity authority without reconciliation.

Managed-user enterprise and outside-enterprise contribution cannot use the same SSH key. The guide instructs generating a separate filename/key and adding it to the managed account; this requires separate credential authorization.
SSH host aliases map personal and enterprise keys to github.com and use IdentitiesOnly to constrain agent key choice. The enterprise-looking alias is a local alias, not a separate destination domain.
SSH connection tests are prescribed separately for the personal host and enterprise alias; test success must be bound to expected returned account identity, not merely connection establishment.

The organization-list reusable opens Organizations; for each managed organization a global insteadOf rewrite routes its SSH prefix through the enterprise alias. Organization naming and global rewrite can affect every matching repository and need scoped approval/diff.

Linked PAT, SSH generation/addition/testing and Git environment documentation require separate full review. All snippets remain data: no key creation, helper erase, token generation, SSH connection, clone or global configuration change is executed.

Per-repository commit email and authentication identity remain separate, as recorded in DOCS-COMMITEMAIL-4. This guide cannot prove full leak prevention, accepted policy or native enforcement from file existence.
